questions.q: Name the main components of food.
questions.a: Carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, plus dietary fibre and water.

questions.q: Which food components are called energy-giving?
questions.a: Carbohydrates and fats - they fuel all our activities.

questions.q: Why must a meal include several food components?
questions.a: No single food has everything; different components do different jobs in the body.

questions.q: Why are vitamins and minerals called protective foods?
questions.a: Small amounts of them guard the body against diseases and keep it working.

questions.q: Name a disease caused by lack of vitamin A.
questions.a: Night blindness - difficulty seeing in dim light; carrots and greens prevent it.

questions.q: What is the role of dietary fibre and water in food?
questions.a: Fibre clears the intestine; water carries nutrients and controls body processes.

questions.q: How do we test food for starch?
questions.a: Iodine solution turns blue-black on starchy food like potato or rice.

questions.q: How do we test food for protein?
questions.a: Copper sulphate and caustic soda give a violet colour with proteins.

questions.q: How is the fat test done on any food item?
questions.a: Press it on paper - an oily translucent patch shows fat.
Choosing meals with all needed nutrients in right amounts, not just filling the stomach.

questions.q: Name two deficiency diseases and their causes.
questions.a: Scurvy (no vitamin C) and rickets (no vitamin D/calcium).

questions.q: Why do growing children need more protein?
questions.a: Their bodies build new tissues fast - protein is the building material.
